sources.title: South Africa's Second Nationally Determined Contribution under the Paris Agreement
sources.temporal_coverage: Recent climate impacts, current vulnerability reporting, adaptation commitments for 2031-2035, and future climate risks.
sources.limitations: National self-report; disaggregated impact data are limited.

sources.title: 3 Sector Climate Readiness Study: Consolidated Workshop Report
sources.organization: Presidential Climate Commission; prepared by OneWorld Sustainable Investments
sources.temporal_coverage: Sector adaptation-readiness workshops and synthesis, with discussion of current capacity and institutional arrangements.
sources.methodology: PCC workshop synthesis of sector presentations and group discussions.

sources.title: Cape Winelands District Municipality Risk Profile Report
sources.organization: Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), GreenBook
sources.temporal_coverage: Vulnerability indices for 1996 and 2011; climate baselines and modeled drought, flood and water-supply risks through 2050.
sources.methodology: GIS model using secondary indicators, hazard data and settlement projections.
sources.limitations: Not locally surveyed; social indicators are dated; water estimates omit reticulation condition.

sources.title: Weather and Crime—Cautious evidence from South Africa
sources.organization: Jorg Ankel-Peters, Anna Bruederle and Gareth Roberts; Q Open
sources.temporal_coverage: Monthly crime and weather observations from January 2001 to March 2012.
sources.methodology: Peer-reviewed reduced-form study of monthly police crime records and gridded weather across 1,158 wards, using an SPEI drought measure.
sources.limitations: Weather, not anthropogenic climate, is studied; effects are subtle, no mediation analysis is conducted, and monthly data limit mechanism interpretation.

claims.locator: NDC printed pp. 5-6, section 2(c), 'Climate impacts experienced in South Africa'.
claims.paraphrase: The NDC reports recent floods in KwaZulu-Natal, Eastern and Western Cape; Northern Cape/interior heatwaves; droughts in Eastern Cape, Western Cape and Free State; Gauteng storms and Western Cape wildfires. Poor communities suffered most; businesses and municipalities struggled to recover.

claims.locator: NDC printed pp. 5-6, section 2(c), household-level vulnerability discussion.
claims.paraphrase: The NDC identifies high household climate vulnerability in KwaZulu-Natal, North West, Limpopo and Eastern Cape; eastern Eastern Cape municipalities are more vulnerable. Unsafe water/toilet access and food poverty are prominent.
affected_groups: households with unsafe water or toilet access

claims.locator: NDC printed p. 7, section 3(a), adaptation strategy and planning arrangements.
claims.paraphrase: The 2024 Climate Change Act establishes recurring climate-risk and vulnerability assessments, adaptation planning and reporting for national, provincial and municipal government and identified sectors.

claims.locator: NDC printed p. 10, Table 1, adaptation Goal 2 and priority interventions for 2031-2035.
claims.paraphrase: For 2031-2035, Goal 2 proposes improved disaster, health and sanitation services, especially in informal settlements; emergency accommodation for flood-displaced marginalized groups and care support for children, older and disabled people.
claims.limitations: Proposal only; no municipality or delivery outcome is named.

claims.locator: Workshop report printed p. 9, section 2.3, 'Key workshop outcomes'.
claims.paraphrase: Workshop synthesis says climate risks were not perceived among municipalities' top ten priorities, making climate response difficult to prioritize amid pressing governance issues.
claims.limitations: Workshop synthesis, not a representative survey.

claims.locator: Workshop report printed p. 13, 'Key issues facing agriculture in dealing with climate change'.
claims.paraphrase: A sector report presented to participants identified water and land stress as compounding climate impacts for smallholder and household producers reliant on rainfall, marginal land, inputs and finance.
claims.limitations: Workshop relays a sector report, not a farmer survey.

claims.locator: Workshop report printed pp. 24-25, built-environment synthesis presentation.
claims.paraphrase: The built-environment presentation says informal settlements and systems fall outside formal controls intended to protect people from hazards such as floodlines; poorer, more vulnerable communities live in these areas.
claims.limitations: Presentation summary; no settlement exposure measurement.

claims.locator: Workshop report printed p. 36, delivery-capacity group discussion summary.
claims.paraphrase: Participants highlighted community-based organizations for their direct local interface and knowledge of realities facing poorer and more vulnerable people as potential adaptation-readiness partners.
claims.limitations: Potential only; CBO results are not evaluated.

claims.locator: Risk profile printed p. 20, section 2.1.2, settlement vulnerability descriptions.
claims.paraphrase: De Doorns and Touwsrivier score very high socioeconomic vulnerability; Touwsrivier also ranks worst for Breede Valley connectivity.

claims.locator: Risk profile printed p. 40, Figure 20 and accompanying text, settlement flood-risk projection.
claims.paraphrase: Under RCP 8.5, increased future flood risk is projected for Paarl, Stellenbosch, De Doorns, Touwsrivier and Montagu.
claims.scenario: RCP 8.5; the settlement risk matrix compares hazard with projected rainfall change toward the 2050s.
claims.limitations: Model combines hazard and rainfall projections; not an event forecast.

claims.locator: Risk profile printed p. 44, Table 3, current local water supply vulnerability.
claims.paraphrase: The profile's 2017-based table gives Witzenberg demand of 146.71 litres per capita daily against 144.23 supply, with a vulnerability score of 1.02.
claims.limitations: Underlying Department of Water and Sanitation data are from 2017.

claims.locator: Risk profile printed p. 45, Witzenberg subsection on water-supply vulnerability.
claims.paraphrase: Witzenberg's water vulnerability score is projected to rise to 1.7 by 2050 with population pressure, declining rainfall and runoff, and increased evaporation.
claims.scenario: Emissions pathway unspecified in cited projection.
claims.limitations: Model combines climate and population; reticulation condition excluded.

claims.paraphrase: A 2001-12 monthly police-ward panel associates warmer months with more violent crime and growing-season droughts with modest increases in rural property-taking crime, not urban crime.
claims.limitations: This is weather, not anthropogenic climate attribution; effects are subtle, mechanisms are not identified, and monthly data miss within-month timing.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The article links weather, especially temperature, to violent crime and growing-season drought to rural property-taking crime; it does not test climate-change attribution or organized conflict.

search_audit.query: South Africa subnational climate vulnerability provincial municipal drought flood heat official climate risk assessment report PDF
search_audit.outcome: Read the 2025 NDC and 2023 Cape Winelands district profile. Verified provincial vulnerability comparisons and named-settlement social, flood and water examples in primary report text.

search_audit.query: South Africa climate change conflict violence protest climate security water drought official report primary source
search_audit.outcome: Found a peer-reviewed weather-crime study with cautious temperature/violent-crime and drought/property-crime results. It does not test anthropogenic climate attribution or organized conflict; no direct climate-conflict claim was verified in the reports read.

search_audit.query: South Africa conflict violence land inequality climate adaptation constraint displacement flood drought adaptation government report
search_audit.outcome: No South Africa-specific primary source-stated conflict, violence or protest pathway constraining climate adaptation was located. PCC workshop material reports governance and delivery-capacity concerns, not conflict-linked constraints.

search_audit.query: South Africa municipal climate resilience capacity adaptation local government community-based organizations early warning official report
search_audit.outcome: NDC documents a multilevel adaptation-planning mandate and proposed 2031-2035 measures; PCC workshops identify municipal prioritization and community-based organizations. These are mandates, proposals and participant reports, not measured delivery outcomes.

gaps: No country-specific source-stated climate-change-to-organized-conflict or conflict-to-adaptation-constraint pathway was verified. The accessible crime study concerns weather and crime, not anthropogenic climate attribution.

A 2024 South Africa Biennial Transparency Report and two relevant World Bank PDFs were discoverable, but direct PDF reading failed at the web reader's 10 MiB limit; indexed passages were not used as evidence.

The most granular local vulnerability profile found was for Cape Winelands; it relies on dated 1996/2011 social indicators, 2017 water data and modeled future risk, so it does not provide a current nationwide municipal comparison.
